subject: LLM data encryption & key ownership options - post-call recap
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@pillarfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: LL M data encryption & key ownership options - post-call recap

Amanda — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call + concrete next steps so your security and procurement teams have something to work from.

Summary of what we covered:
- Scope: Pillar will send low-volume PII-enriched transaction payloads to an LLM endpoint for risk-scoring and enrichment. No long-term storage of raw requests is planned, but you do keep derived scores in your DB.
- Residency: Primary region is us-west-2. Pillar also has an EU entity; team asked about future EU-only deployments.
- Retention & logging: Security asked for request/response logging for 12 months, with the ability to redact PII before long-term storage.
- Encryption asks: In-transit TLS required (mTLS preferred for service-to-service); at-rest encryption AES-256; desire for customer-managed keys (BYOK) with an HSM-backed KMS and proof of key origin/control.

Redwood capabilities (short):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with optional mTLS between customer VPC and Redwood Private; hosted API uses strong TLS + cert pinning.
- At-rest: all customer data stored encrypted; we support provider-managed keys by default, and customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS with CloudHSM root) for Dedicated and Private.
- BYOK/HSM options: 1) BYOK using AWS KMS with imported keys (subject to your KMS policy), 2) CloudHSM-backed KMS where HSM root holds key material, 3) On-prem HSM integration for Redwood Private (air-gapped options).
- Logging: request/response logging is configurable; we can provide redaction hooks and deliver logs to your S3 or Splunk with field-level masking.

Open questions for your security/procurement teams (please confirm):
1) Do you require the HSM to be the ultimate root of trust (no ability for Redwood or cloud provider to export key material)?
2) Are you comfortable with cloud KMS + CloudHSM (AWS) or do you need an on-prem HSM?
3) For logs, do you want raw responses retained behind your key, or should Redwood apply redaction/pseudonymization before export?

Requested deliverables (what I will send by EOD):
- Encryption matrix comparing options (attached: redwood-encryption-matrix-v1.xlsx)
- Short BYOK runbook + implementation notes (attached draft: redwood-byok-runbook-draft.md)
- Proposed SOW wording for Dedicated/Private if you prefer HSM-backed keys in prod (I'll draft after we agree scope)

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Pillar security to share the completed security questionnaire (you mentioned Procure would attach) — Amanda
- Redwood to send matrix + runbook — Sofia (attached)
- If Pillar wants HSM-rooted BYOK, schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (Redwood infra) to scope feasibility and timeline — SOON (Karthik to coordinate)

If you'd like I can also include a short architecture sketch showing where keys live in each option (cloud/KMS vs CloudHSM vs Private HSM).

Thanks again — happy to jump on a follow-up with your security lead this week.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-encryption-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-byok-runbook-draft.md (text)

From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@pillarfin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procure Team <procure@pillarfin.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LL M data encryption & key ownership options - post-call recap

Thanks Sofia, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Our security team does require that the root key material be HSM-protected and non-exportable by the cloud provider or vendor if we choose the HSM-rooted BYOK option.
- We prefer CloudHSM-backed KMS in AWS for initial rollouts (us-west-2) because that aligns with our infra. On-prem HSM is an option but will require a longer procurement timeline.
- For logs: we want request/response retention for 12 months, but PII fields must be redacted before stored long-term. Short-term raw logs (30 days) can be retained for debugging and then purged or wrapped under our keys for long-term analysis.

I attached the initial security questionnaire — it's not complete but will help you triage. Also: procurement wants to understand whether Redwood can sign an addendum confirming you will not have access to the decrypted customer data when BYOK is used.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports mTLS to the endpoint (we prefer mutual auth for service-to-service traffic)?

Thanks,
Amanda
Senior Security PM, Pillar Financial
amanda.lee@pillarfin.com

Thanks for the context — quick technical notes (summary + constraints):

1) CloudHSM-backed KMS (AWS) — supported: we can integrate with an AWS KMS customer master key that has CloudHSM as the root. In that configuration the HSM holds the key material and AWS KMS enforces non-exportability. Redwood will never be able to export the root key. We use envelope encryption: requests are encrypted client-side under a data key which is wrapped by your KMS CMK.

2) mTLS: supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated via a VPC peering/sidecar model. For hosted API we support TLS and client certs for service-to-service flows if you route through our dedicated ingress (we'll need to provision client certs and a CA trust; we can manage cert rotation if you prefer).

3) Logging + redaction:
- We can stream logs to your S3 bucket encrypted under your CMK; for long-term retention we recommend hooking a Lambda that strips/redacts PII fields before moving to long-term storage.
- Alternatively, Redwood can perform configurable field-level redaction before log export; note this will require shipping a redaction spec and test vectors.

4) On-prem HSM / Private: available but requires a Private deployment. That path is feasible if you need an air-gapped HSM or a direct on-prem appliance. Longer procurement and onboarding timeline (estimate 8–12 weeks for infra + integration work).

5) Limitations / notes:
- Streaming KV cache: we do not persist unencrypted KV cache to disk; under BYOK scenario we encrypt cache layers under the same CMK wrapping strategy.
- We cannot sign an addendum that prevents Redwood from ever accessing decrypted data if there are valid emergency operational needs unless Pillar assumes a Private deployment with strict policies — in AWS KMS model Redwood as operator can have access to the environment (but not the root key material). We can, however, include contractual controls and audit hooks (KMS key usage logs, CloudTrail, and proof of no-export).

Suggested immediate next steps:
- I will upload an architecture sketch to the shared Drive and a technical appendix describing the KMS/CloudHSM flow (link below).
- Karthik: please propose 2x slots for a 45m technical call with Pillar security. I can join to present the BYOK runbook.

Links / attachments: redwood-byok-runbook-draft.md (attached), architecture sketch: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3ExampleWhitepaper

If Amanda/procurement want a sample addendum language, legal can draft a vendor BYOK clause for review — that tends to speed procurement.

—
